stories.head: Adobe Brings Agentic AI to the Content Supply Chain with CX Enterprise Coworker
stories.plain: Adobe is embedding an agentic AI coworker directly into its content supply chain, letting teams automate creation, approval, and delivery of personalised content at scale. This matters because it signals a major platform shift — Adobe is no longer just a creative tool but an autonomous content operator, which will reshape how enterprise marketing stacks are bought and evaluated.

stories.head: Data Governance More Than Triples AI ROI Success, Convertr Research Finds
stories.plain: New research shows 84% of teams with strong data governance meet or exceed AI ROI targets, versus only 27% of teams with governance gaps. This is a critical buying signal: organisations evaluating AI tools now need to treat governance infrastructure as a prerequisite, not an afterthought, or risk wasting their AI investment entirely.

stories.head: G2's CPTO on How AI Agents Now Build B2B Shortlists Using Third-Party Evidence
stories.plain: G2's chief product and technology officer explains that AI agents constructing B2B purchase shortlists trust third-party review evidence over vendor positioning. This directly changes how software vendors must market themselves — your own messaging matters less; what review platforms say about you matters more. A must-read for anyone planning a 2027 martech budget.

stories.head: G2 Unifies Four Software Marketplaces to Power Answer Engine Optimization in the Agentic Era
stories.plain: G2 is merging G2, Capterra, Software Advice, and GetApp into one platform focused on answer engine optimization, letting brands control how AI systems cite and recommend them across the biggest B2B review networks. As agentic buyers replace human searchers, being visible in AI-generated answers is becoming a core marketing discipline.

stories.head: Built to Adapt: Why Composable Martech Is Becoming the New Standard
stories.plain: Coverage from the November MarTech Conference argues that composable, modular stacks are replacing monolithic suites as the preferred architecture for AI-ready marketing. The key insight: composability reduces vendor lock-in and lets teams swap in new AI components without rebuilding everything — directly relevant to anyone making martech purchasing decisions heading into 2027.

stories.head: Data Governance More Than Triples AI ROI Success, Convertr Research Finds
stories.plain: New Convertr research shows 84% of teams with strong data governance meet or beat their AI ROI targets, versus only 27% of teams with governance gaps. This is a striking, concrete number that changes how buyers justify AI spend and how vendors sell data-quality tools — governance is no longer a compliance checkbox, it's a revenue lever.

stories.head: Adobe Brings Agentic AI to the Content Supply Chain with CX Enterprise Coworker
stories.plain: Adobe is embedding an agentic AI 'coworker' into its content supply chain, letting autonomous agents accelerate creation and delivery of personalised content at scale. This matters because it signals that a Tier-1 martech vendor is shipping agentic decisioning inside a production content workflow — not just a demo — which will pressure competitors and reshape how brands staff creative operations.

stories.head: From journeys to decisions: The next era of customer engagement
stories.plain: Coverage from the November MarTech Conference argues that static pre-planned journeys are being replaced by real-time AI decisioning that picks the next best action per person. This reframes how CEPs are bought and built — the architecture shifts from campaign orchestration to continuous, per-person decision loops, with big implications for platform selection and team skills.

stories.head: G2's CPTO on how AI agents now build B2B shortlists — and why third-party evidence beats your own positioning
stories.plain: G2's CPTO explains that AI agents constructing purchase shortlists trust third-party review signals over vendor self-promotion. This directly changes how software marketers allocate budget — earned review content and ratings on third-party sites now influence AI-driven buying decisions before a human ever sees a website, making GEO and review strategy essential.

stories.head: Claritas brings live optimization to acquisition email
stories.plain: Claritas launched a product that adjusts email audiences and subject lines in real time while a campaign is still running, then uses holdouts and attribution to measure lift. This is a practical bandit/RL-style capability shipped inside a mainstream acquisition channel, showing that live adaptive optimization is moving from experimentation platforms into everyday email tools.

themes.head: The Agentic Shortlist: AI Agents Now Pick Your Vendors
body: AI agents are increasingly making or heavily influencing B2B software shortlists, pulling from third-party review sites and structured evidence rather than vendor positioning pages. G2's move to consolidate four marketplaces is a direct bet that the data layer AI agents trust will decide purchase outcomes before a human ever enters the funnel.

This flips classic demand-generation logic: being findable by an AI agent matters as much as being persuasive to a human buyer. Marketers must now optimize for machine-readable credibility signals — reviews, benchmarks, and structured brand context — not just ad copy or landing-page conversion.
ev: Agile Brand · G2 & the agentic shortlist
MarTech Series · Marcora brand context for AI tools

themes.head: Data Governance as the Real AI Multiplier
body: Convertr research shows that strong data governance more than triples AI ROI success rates, making clean, well-managed data the single highest-leverage investment a marketing team can make before layering on AI tooling. The bottleneck is not the model — it is the data feeding it.

This theme connects directly to budget pressure: 61% of marketers face C-suite demands to prove AI ROI, yet many are paying premiums for data sets they cannot operationalize. Composable martech architectures are rising partly because they make it easier to govern and swap data layers without rebuilding the entire stack.
ev: MarTech Series · Convertr data governance research
MarTech · Don't pay for data you can't use

themes.head: Agentic AI Inside the Stack: From Copilot to Coworker
body: Adobe's CX Enterprise Coworker, Typeform's integration with ChatGPT & Claude, and Impartner's Aimi Analytics all represent the same structural shift: AI is moving from a bolt-on assistant to an embedded agent that takes actions inside existing workflows. The integration surface is now the product.

For marketing operators this means evaluating tools not just on features but on how well they expose actions to external AI agents. Platforms that sit behind closed APIs will increasingly lose ground to those that publish skills or connectors into the emerging agent ecosystems built around large language models.
ev: MarTech Series · Typeform in ChatGPT & Claude

themes.head: Composable Architecture Replaces the Suite
body: Composable martech — assembling best-of-breed components rather than buying a monolithic suite — is shifting from an edge practice to the mainstream default. The logic is now explicitly tied to AI: rigid suites cannot swap in new AI models or data sources fast enough to keep pace with the technology cycle.

Liferay's governance-first CMS launch and the rise of curated data partnerships like AudienceMix & Alliant reflect the same composable pattern at the content and data layers. Decision-makers are being advised to audit whether their current stack can be decomposed before signing multi-year suite contracts.
ev: MarTech · Composable martech becoming the standard
MarTech · What to do before buying a martech platform

themes.head: Measuring What AI Actually Earns: From Productivity to Provable ROI
body: Productivity gains from AI are real but do not automatically show up in revenue metrics, and C-suites are losing patience with efficiency arguments. Research flagged this month shows that the gap between AI activity and attributable business outcomes is now the defining tension in marketing budget negotiations for 2027.

Multi-touch attribution alone is not enough; teams are pairing Marketing Mix Modeling with post-purchase surveys to get a defensible read on true incrementality. The parallel finding that ChatGPT paid traffic converts far worse than Google traffic underscores that channel & model selection must now be evaluated on outcome quality, not just volume.

month.takeaway: Every major move this month — agentic coworkers, composable stacks, data governance mandates, AI-driven shortlists — ultimately forces the same decision: prove that AI spending creates measurable business value or lose budget to teams that can.
